topics.title: 146.520 MHz FM (2 m national simplex calling)
topics.summary: Widely recognized North American amateur radio FM simplex calling frequency on 2 meters.
topics.overview: 146.520 MHz is commonly used as a national FM simplex calling frequency in the amateur 2-meter band. SignalTerrain frequency topics capture purpose, band context, and listening notes — not private traffic content.
topics.historicalContext: Calling frequencies exist to help operators find each other; local practice varies. Always follow license rules and band plans.
knownFacts: Mode context: FM voice simplex calling (amateur).
unknowns: Local activity level is not measured in this foundation demo.
Repeater vs simplex etiquette varies by region.
watchFor: Propagation and local net schedules that change usefulness of a calling frequency.

verification.limitations: Not a substitute for your local band plan or license conditions.

waypointAnalysis.text: Frequency topics should stay practical and lawful. Pair them with propagation context so listeners understand why a quiet night might be conditions — not a broken radio.

topics.title: Sample HF propagation note (disturbed)
topics.summary: Educational note that elevated space weather can disturb HF paths for amateur and shortwave listeners.
topics.overview: Propagation topics explain how ionospheric conditions change what operators hear. This sample describes a disturbed HF window in plain language and links to space-weather awareness — without fabricating a live NOAA product.
topics.historicalContext: Operators have long compared quiet and disturbed days; modern digests should cite space-weather bulletins when available.

timeline.text: Illustrative disturbed period for demo graph.

knownFacts: Geomagnetic activity can alter HF propagation.
This record is a teaching sample, not a forecast.
watchFor: Official space-weather bulletins when connectors exist.
VHF openings that sometimes accompany unsettled conditions.

confidence.rationale: No live bulletin bound to this sample.

waypointAnalysis.text: Propagation notes belong beside frequency topics. The goal is expectation-setting for listeners — calm, specific, and honest about what was not measured.
